questions.question: At its core, how does an LLM write an answer?
options: It looks the answer up in a database of facts
It predicts the next piece of text, over and over, until the answer is done
It copies the closest matching web page
It runs a separate program written for each type of question
questions.explanation: An LLM generates text one token at a time by predicting what comes next. Doing that well is what lets it write, summarize and reason.

questions.question: Why can an LLM give a confident answer that is wrong?
options: It is designed to mislead users
It only works when connected to the internet
It produces text that sounds right based on patterns, and it sounds just as sure when the details are wrong
It always has a bug in its first answer
questions.explanation: The model doesn't check facts. It writes plausible text, and the tone is the same whether the details are right or wrong. These errors are often called hallucinations.

questions.question: You want an accurate answer about your company's travel policy. What helps most?
options: Use a longer, more polite question
Paste in the policy and ask the model to quote the sections it relies on
Tell the model it is an expert
questions.explanation: The model has never seen your private documents. Giving it the source, and asking it to point to where its answer came from, makes the answer grounded and easy to check.

questions.question: What does fine-tuning add after pre-training?
options: Knowledge of events after the training cutoff
The ability to follow instructions and act as a helpful assistant
questions.explanation: Pre-training teaches language and general knowledge. Fine-tuning, including feedback from people, teaches the model to follow instructions, answer directly and decline harmful requests.
